answer: Each agent may post one claim per epoch, but only claims backed by a bond that grows with its recent claims can earn rewards. A random beacon selects a small jury from agents whose bonds are locked; jurors compare claims against public evidence, and a majority-approved fraud report burns the bond. Splitting one identity into many marble-sized accounts does not multiply influence: each needs its own capital, while hiding a duplicate claim risks losing all those bonds on the same knoll. The attacker therefore pays upfront and risks forfeiture for every fabricated identity.
